body: [A10] Raised out of a review of PR #428 (issue #413), which measured it and correctly declared it outside that lane. ## What is wrong `scripts/gen_toc.py` decides where a fenced code block and a type-1 HTML block end by reading Python's notion of whitespace, which is wider than the one the renderer applies. Two decisions are affected, both present at the current dev tip and unchanged by #413: - the closing fence, at the `not m.group(2).strip()` test: CommonMark 4.5 allows only spaces or tabs after a closing fence sequence, and `str.strip()` also removes 25 other characters (line tabulation, form feed, U+001C to U+001F, U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000 to U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F and U+3000). - the type-1 end condition, at the `` pattern: end condition 1 of CommonMark 4.6 names ``, ``, `` and ``, with nothing but the tag inside, and `\s` again admits the same 25. ## What it costs A heading placed after a closing fence that carries one of those characters, or after ``, is listed in the generated contents while the renderer leaves it inside the block and shows no heading. The reviewer measured 25 rows for the fence and 27 for the type-1 case, plus one carriage-return row, all against the live renderer, and the behaviour is identical at the base of #428 and at its head. That is the escape direction: a contents entry, an anchor and, through the em-dash gate's provenance exemption, a waiver for a label mirrored from a heading the page does not render. ## Why it is not urgent No tracked page carries any of the 25 characters, and none carries the shapes at all, so nothing on the tree is affected today. There is also no gate that keeps those characters out of Markdown: the hygiene populations exclude Markdown and the documentation scrub has no such rule. So the escape is reachable by any future page. ## Acceptance 1. Each of the two decisions reads the class the renderer applies at that position, or the walk refuses input it cannot answer for, naming file, line and character. 2. Whichever is chosen is held by an arm that fails when the class is narrowed back, one arm per position. 3. The rows the review measured (the fence rows and the type-1 rows, including the carriage-return row) agree with the renderer or fall in a family declared in the source and in the documentation with its direction and its measured boundary. 4. The same sweep is run at the base to show the change moves only these rows. ## Notes This sits next to #437 and next to the same family inside #413, which is closing its own positions in its own lane. Whoever takes this should read the round-9 review on PR #428 first: it names the exact lines, the character set and the row counts, and its sweep tool is the instrument to reuse.

comments.body: [A10] Widening this issue's scope, from a measurement in the round-9 review of PR #428 (published there). The issue as written treats the fence and type-1 closers as one family: positions where the walk reads Python's notion of whitespace and the renderer reads spaces and tabs. At the type-1 closers there are two more row families, and neither is a whitespace divergence at all. **Blanks inside the closing tag.** The renderer ends a type-1 block only on a line containing the literal ``, ``, `` or ``. The walk ends it on a pattern that admits a run of whitespace before the closing angle bracket, so `` and `` end the block for the walk and do not end it for the renderer. The review measured these through the shipped gate at the base, at the round-8 head and at the round-9 head: each stays exempt, and the renderer shows no such heading. **Case folding.** The walk matches the closing name case-insensitively under Python's Unicode rules, where the renderer folds ASCII only. Under Python's rules `s` also matches U+017F and `i` also matches U+0131 and U+0130, so a closing tag spelled with those characters ends the block for the walk alone. The review measured two such rows end to end, and they are in no issue today. **What changes here.** The acceptance stays as written, with the measured rows extended: the fence rows and the type-1 rows this issue already names, plus the blank-inside-the-tag rows and the case-folded rows. Whichever answer is chosen, reading the renderer's class or refusing what the walk cannot answer for, it has to cover all four families, and the arms have to fail when any one of them is narrowed back. Nothing on the tree is affected today: no tracked page carries any of these shapes, and the same was true when the issue was raised.
